newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q2 GDP shows slowing growth in economy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q2 GDP shows slowing growth in economy.

text.p: Second quarter gross domestic product (GDP) posted a slightly higher-than-expected growth rate of 2.2 percent, but the bond market rallied nonetheless as the deflator index was up only 1.4 percent.
In addition, first quarter GDP growth was revised downward by a full point to 4.9 percent.

Economists surveyed by Reuters had been expecting a rise of 1.9 percent in the second quarter. However, the expected slowdown in the second quarter and revision of first quarter growth was widely regarded as giving the Federal Reserve room to hold off on further tightening of monetary policy.
The Fed hiked short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at its March meeting of the policymaking Federal Open Market Committee, but the same body left rates unchanged at its May and July meetings.

Fred Sturm, economist at Fuji Securities Inc, said the number was in line with expectations and the downward revision for the first quarter was welcomed by the bond market. However, he added that revisions from more than a quarter-ago were largely ancient history for most traders, he said.
Lynn Reaser, chief economist at Barnett Bank Inc, said there was a notable decline in consumer spending.
"It's very confusing with the benchmark revisions. The Street is struggling to make sense out of this," said Brian Wesbury, chief economist with Griffin, Kubik, Stephens & Thompson Inc.
With the price deflator index up only 1.4 percent -- its smallest gain since the second quarter of 1964 -- inflation appeared to remain well contained, Wesbury said.
However, he said that going back to the 1993 to 1995 period, there was little difference year-to-year in growth, but some wild swings quarter-to-quarter.
The economy did grow faster in 1996, he said.
